All three tasks complete. Here's what I found.

## 1. Development API vs `api/openapi-v1.json` — GET only

**Result: conformant.** 15/15 documented GET operations pass (v2 base at `http://localhost:4300`, `include_unsafe: false` — the 12 POST/PUT/DELETE operations were correctly skipped).

| Operation | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/health | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /api/users | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /api/users/{id} | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /api/products | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /api/products/{id} | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /api/orders | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /api/categories | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /api/notifications | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /ajax/get · /ajax/slow · /ajax/sse | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /ajax/fail/{code} | 500 | ✅ (documented 5XX) |
| GET /tables/data | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /forms/cascade | 200 | ✅ |
| GET /files/download/{type} | 200 | ✅ |

**Two caveats worth your attention:**

- **My first run had 5 false failures** — `path "id": "{{id}}" must be integer`, etc. Those were the `Playground API` collection's unresolved placeholders (`{{id}}`, `{{code}}`, `{{type}}`), not API defects. Re-running with concrete params (`id=1, code=500, type=csv, page=1`) turned all 5 green. If you run this in CI, the collection needs those variables set in the Development environment.
- **The pass is shallow.** In v1 most operations declare only a description — no `schema`, no `content` — e.g. `GET /api/users` → `200: "Array of users"`. So "pass" means *status is documented*, not that the body shape is validated. Only `/api/health` and `/api/reset` carry a content example.

Reports: `.testver/contracts/v1-get-only.json`, `.testver/contracts/v1-get-only-params.json`

## 2. `openapi-v1.json` → `openapi-v2.json` — what breaks

**2 breaking changes:**

| Breaking | Detail | Client impact |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/products` | **new REQUIRED** query param `page` (integer) | Every existing caller omitting `page` is now spec-invalid; strict clients/gateways will reject or 400 |
| `GET /api/categories` | **operation removed** | Any consumer of the category list breaks outright |

**Also changed but not flagged as breaking:**
- `GET /api/products/{id}` path param `id`: `integer` → `string`. Loosening for clients, but a server-side type-contract change — worth confirming the provider now parses string ids.
- Version bumped `1.0.0` → `2.0.0`.

**Important:** I checked both breaking changes against the *running* Development API — it **still serves `GET /api/categories` with 200** and **still accepts `GET /api/products` without `page`**. So v2 is a spec-only change today; the deployed service has not implemented either change yet. You have a window before v2 consumers hit a non-conforming provider.

## 3. Pact contract from Product lookup — verified

The `Product lookup` folder lives inside the broader `Playground API` collection, and `api_pact_generate` scopes by collection, so I built a scoped consumer collection **`Product Lookup`** containing exactly those two calls, then generated from it:

- `pacts/product-lookup-playground-api.json` — consumer `product-lookup` → provider `playground-api`, Pact **v3.0.0**, 2 interactions
  - `List products and extract first id` → `GET /api/products`
  - `Get product by productId` → `GET /api/products/1`

**Verification against the Development API: 2/2 interactions verified ✅**

**One limitation to fix if this contract matters:** the generated `matchingRules` only contain a **root-level** `{"match":"type"}` at `$`. That pins "the response is an array / an object" but does **not** pin the product object's fields — so a rename of `sku`, or dropping `featured`, would not be caught. The literal field values are still in the contract body, but they're the only coupling. To make it a real schema contract, add per-field type matchers (or generate against the v1 spec's schemas — which, per the caveat above, barely exist). Say the word and I'll tighten it.

One housekeeping note: my `Product Lookup` working collection has a leftover validation rule `$[0].id exists` on `Get product by productId` (a mis-scoped rule I added before seeing that endpoint returns a single object, not an array). It's inert for the Pact run, but it will report a false failure if anyone runs that request in a chain — there's no tool to delete a single rule, so it needs removing in the UI.

**Not done, and why:** no test *scripts* were written (you asked for checks, not automation), and I did not run v2's contract check since v2 isn't what's deployed. Want me to (a) tighten the Pact matchers to field level, or (b) contract-check the Dev API against **v2** to quantify the gap before the release?

messages.content: Run "Get product by id" from the Playground API collection once for each row of api/products.csv against Development: each row gives the id, the status to expect, and the expected name. Then try /ajax/fail with 400, 401, 404 and 500 and check each one returns that status with an error message.

## 1. Data-driven run — "Get product by id" × `api/products.csv` (Development)

`api_run_data_driven` on the saved request `req-1793077387563-d0h9-rr` (`{{baseUrl}}/api/products/{{id}}`, env `Development` → `http://localhost:4300`):

**4/4 rows passed**

| Row | id | expected_status | Result | Body `$.name` | expected_name check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 200 | ✅ 200 | Incredible Wooden Ball | ✅ matches |
| 2 | 2 | 200 | ✅ 200 | Tasty Granite Towels | ✅ matches |
| 3 | 7 | 200 | ✅ 200 | Fantastic Bronze Tuna | ✅ matches |
| 4 | 99999 | 404 | ✅ 404 (`{"error":"not found"}`) | — | n/a (blank) |

One caveat worth knowing: the runner only enforces the `expected_status` column — `expected_name` came in as a variable but there is no validation on the request, so a renamed product would **not** have failed the run. I verified the three names by re-issuing rows 1–3 individually (output above) — all three really do return the expected names, so the data is correct today.

## 2. Unused column vs. verification
To make the name check real rather than eyeballed, the request needs a `body-json-path` validation on `$.name` with `operator: equals`, `expected: {{expected_name}}`. Say the word and I'll add it (I haven't, since you didn't ask for the request to be modified).

## 3. Forced HTTP errors — `/ajax/fail/{code}`

Saved request is `{{baseUrl}}/ajax/fail/{{code}}`; I called each resolved URL.

| Code | Status returned | `content-type` | Body | Error message present |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | 400 Bad Request | application/json | `{"error":"Forced HTTP 400"}` | ✅ |
| 401 | 401 Unauthorized | application/json | `{"error":"Forced HTTP 401"}` | ✅ |
| 404 | 404 Not Found | application/json | `{"error":"Forced HTTP 404"}` | ✅ |
| 500 | 500 Internal Server Error | application/json | `{"error":"Forced HTTP 500"}` | ✅ |

All four behave correctly: the status echoes the requested code, the body is JSON and the `error` string names the code. Responses were 1–5 ms, so no timeout concerns.

**Two notes on what the error contract does *not* do:** 401 returns no `WWW-Authenticate` header and no `Retry-After` on 500 — fine for a test playground, but if this endpoint is ever a template for a real service, those headers are the usual expectation.

Next natural step: add the `$.name = {{expected_name}}` validation to "Get product by id" so the CSV's third column is actually enforced — want me to?

`http://localhost:4300/api/health` (the Development environment's `baseUrl` in the **Playground API** collection) was healthy immediately — 1 check, 0.0s.

## 2. Mock
Started from `api/openapi-v1.json` — **28 routes** = the 27 operations the spec defines, plus my `GET /api/products/{id}` override, since routes take precedence over spec-generated ones. Listening at `http://127.0.0.1:63408`.

## 3. The three calls

| # | Request | Status | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GET /api/products/7` | `503 Service Unavailable` | `{"error":"Service Unavailable"}` |
| 2 | `GET /api/products/7` | `503 Service Unavailable` | `{"error":"Service Unavailable"}` |

## 2. `openapi-v1.json` → `openapi-v2.json` — what breaks

**2 breaking changes** (clients written against v1 will fail):

| Breaking change | Detail | Client impact |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/products` | `page` query parameter is now **required** (`type: integer`) | Any v1 client calling `/api/products` with no query string gets a request the v2 spec rejects — contract violation, and a compliant v2 server will 400 it |
| `/api/categories` | **operation removed** (`GET /api/categories` no longer exists in v2) | Callers get 404; the Categories tag remains in v2 but has no operation |

Additional differences the diff did not classify as breaking, but worth knowing:
- `GET /api/products/{id}` – `id` path parameter changed **integer → string**. This is a widening, so it is non-breaking for callers, but any strict validator pinning `integer` (schemas, generated clients) will now flag it.
- **The live Development server still behaves as v1**: `GET /api/products` returned 200 with no `page`, and `GET /api/categories` returned 200 — the running service does not yet enforce the v2 contract. Deploying v2 is a real cutover for clients.

- Pact v3 written to **`pacts/product-lookup-web-testver-playground-api.json`** — consumer `product-lookup-web`, provider `testver-playground-api`, 2 interactions, bodies matched **by type** (not by today's values).

## 2. `openapi-v1.json` → `openapi-v2.json` — what breaks

**2 breaking changes** (clients written against v1 will fail):

| Breaking change | Detail | Client impact |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/products` | `page` query parameter is now **required** (`type: integer`) | Any v1 client calling `/api/products` with no query string gets a request the v2 spec rejects — contract violation, and a compliant v2 server will 400 it |
| `/api/categories` | **operation removed** (`GET /api/categories` no longer exists in v2) | Callers get 404; the Categories tag remains in v2 but has no operation |

Additional differences the diff did not classify as breaking, but worth knowing:
- `GET /api/products/{id}` – `id` path parameter changed **integer → string**. This is a widening, so it is non-breaking for callers, but any strict validator pinning `integer` (schemas, generated clients) will now flag it.
- **The live Development server still behaves as v1**: `GET /api/products` returned 200 with no `page`, and `GET /api/categories` returned 200 — the running service does not yet enforce the v2 contract. Deploying v2 is a real cutover for clients.

## 3. Pact contract from the Product lookup requests → verified

The `Product lookup` folder in *Playground API* contains the two product calls plus an unrelated SSE/slow-endpoint poll step, and `api_pact_generate` runs at collection level, so I scoped the contract to exactly the lookup calls:

- ✅ Get product by captured id → 200

Two honest limitations of this generated contract you should know before leaning on it in CI: the `productId` is pinned as a literal path (`/api/products/1`), so the "get by id" interaction only describes one id; and body comparison is a type match at the body root, so it protects the response *shape*, not per-field presence inside each array element.

messages.content: Run "Get product by id" from the Playground API collection once for each row of api/products.csv against Development: each row gives the id, the status to expect, and the expected name. Then try /ajax/fail with 400, 401, 404 and 500 and check each one returns that status with an error message.

Both runs complete against **Development** (`http://localhost:4300`).

## 1. Get product by id × `api/products.csv` — 4/4 rows passed

| Row | `id` | Expected status | Actual | Expected name | Actual name | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 200 | 200 ✅ | Incredible Wooden Ball | Incredible Wooden Ball ✅ | **pass** |
| 2 | 2 | 200 | 200 ✅ | Tasty Granite Towels | Tasty Granite Towels ✅ | **pass** |
| 3 | 7 | 200 | 200 ✅ | Fantastic Bronze Tuna | Fantastic Bronze Tuna ✅ | **pass** |
| 4 | 99999 | 404 | 404 ✅ | *(empty)* | *(no name — `{"error":"not found"}`)* ✅ | **pass** |

Note on method: `api_run_data_driven` only asserts the `expected_status` column, so I sent each row individually afterwards to also verify `expected_name`. Both dimensions match on all four rows, and the 404 row correctly returns no product body.

## 2. `/ajax/fail/{code}` — 4/4 returned the requested status with an error message

| Code | Status | `content-type` | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `400 Bad Request` ✅ | `application/json` | `{"error":"Forced HTTP 400"}` |
| 401 | `401 Unauthorized` ✅ | `application/json` | `{"error":"Forced HTTP 401"}` |

Run the chain against Development.

Chain created and green against **Development**.

## What was added — `Playground API` → folder `Product lookup`

| Step | Request | Config |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GET {{baseUrl}}/api/products` — "1. List products and capture first id" | Extract `{{productId}}` ← body `$[0].id`; validation status = 200 |
| 2 | `GET {{baseUrl}}/api/products/{{productId}}` — "2. Get product by captured id" | Validations: status = 200, `$.name` equals `Incredible Wooden Ball` |
| 3 | `GET {{baseUrl}}/ajax/slow` — "3. Poll slow endpoint until ok is true" | Validation `$.ok` equals `true`; retry 5× every 1000 ms until validations pass; timeout 30000 ms |

## Run result — environment `Development` (baseUrl `http://localhost:4300`)

```
Chain: Product lookup (3 steps)
✅ Step 1  GET /api/products                 200  3ms      Extracted productId = 1
✅ Step 2  GET /api/products/{{productId}}   200  2ms      (2/2 validations passed)
✅ Step 3  GET /ajax/slow                     200  4019ms   (1/1 validation passed)

Result: 3/3 steps passed
```

Notes on the config:
- **Extraction shape**: `/api/products` returns a **bare JSON array**, so the path is `$[0].id` (not `$.items[0].id`). The captured value flows into step 2's URL as `productId=1`.

messages.content: Import the API spec from http://localhost:4300/api-docs/openapi.json as a collection called "Playground API". Create two environments: Development with baseUrl http://localhost:4300 and Production with baseUrl https://testplay.venomva.com. Then run the health, products and categories requests against Development.

All three requests returned 200 against Development. Import and environment setup are complete.

## Collection: "Playground API"
Imported from `http://localhost:4300/api-docs/openapi.json` — **27 endpoints**, **11 folders** (Health & State, Users, Products, Orders, Categories, Notifications, AJAX scenarios, Tables, Forms, Files, Shop / Cart). Spec cached at `.testver/specs/localhost_4300-openapi.json`.

## Environments created

| Environment | Variable | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Development | `baseUrl` | `http://localhost:4300` |
| Production | `baseUrl` | `https://testplay.venomva.com` |

All requests use `{{baseUrl}}`, so switching environments needs no request edits.

## Runs against Development

| Request | Endpoint | Status | Duration | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Health check | `GET /api/health` | **200 OK** | 4 ms | `{ ok: true, time: "2026-10-27T04:45:47.196Z" }` |
| List products (first 50) | `GET /api/products` | **200 OK** | 2 ms | 18.9 KB array; first item `id:1` "Incredible Wooden Ball", `price:1978`, `categoryId:2`, `featured:true` |
| List categories | `GET /api/categories` | **200 OK** | 2 ms | 8 categories — Electronics, Clothing, Books, Home & Garden, Sports, Toys, Beauty, Automotive (all `parentId: null`) |

Notes:
- Responses are `application/json; charset=utf-8`, served by Express with an `ETag`, and each sets a `connect.sid` cookie — session handling is stateful, so chain runs should reuse the session rather than assume statelessness.
- `GET /api/products` is capped at 50 by the request name; pagination/filtering lives in the `Tables` folder (`GET /tables/data`).

I did not touch Production — say the word if you want these three run there, or want contract checks against the saved spec.

All three requests returned 200 against Development. Import and environment setup are complete.

## Collection: "Playground API"
Imported from `http://localhost:4300/api-docs/openapi.json` — **27 endpoints**, **11 folders** (Health & State, Users, Products, Orders, Categories, Notifications, AJAX scenarios, Tables, Forms, Files, Shop / Cart). Spec cached at `.testver/specs/localhost_4300-openapi.json`.

## Environments created

| Environment | Variable | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Development | `baseUrl` | `http://localhost:4300` |
| Production | `baseUrl` | `https://testplay.venomva.com` |

All requests use `{{baseUrl}}`, so switching environments needs no request edits.

## Runs against Development

| Request | Endpoint | Status | Duration | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Health check | `GET /api/health` | **200 OK** | 4 ms | `{ ok: true, time: "2026-10-27T04:45:47.196Z" }` |
| List products (first 50) | `GET /api/products` | **200 OK** | 2 ms | 18.9 KB array; first item `id:1` "Incredible Wooden Ball", `price:1978`, `categoryId:2`, `featured:true` |
| List categories | `GET /api/categories` | **200 OK** | 2 ms | 8 categories — Electronics, Clothing, Books, Home & Garden, Sports, Toys, Beauty, Automotive (all `parentId: null`) |

Notes:
- Responses are `application/json; charset=utf-8`, served by Express with an `ETag`, and each sets a `connect.sid` cookie — session handling is stateful, so chain runs should reuse the session rather than assume statelessness.
- `GET /api/products` is capped at 50 by the request name; pagination/filtering lives in the `Tables` folder (`GET /tables/data`).

I did not touch Production — say the word if you want these three run there, or want contract checks against the saved spec.
